2. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 66 of 1991 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Additional Court, Dhaka impleading the opposite party No. 1 as defendant No. 1 and other opposite parties as other defendants praying for declaration that the judgment and decree dated 5.6.1980 passed in Title suit No. 346 of 1977 by the First Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka is illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff. The plaintiff alleged that the suit land originally belonged to Priaya Nath Basak and others and on the death of Priaya Nath Basak, his sons Nipendra Nath Basak, Nagendra Nath Basak, Bhupendra Nath Basak and Digendra Nath Basak became the owners of the suit land to the extent of 4 annas shares each and their names were correctly recorded in the S.A. Khatian and that during the war of liberation between India and Pakistan in 1965 the aforesaid S.A. recorded owners left the country for India and the suit land was declared and treated as enemy property and subsequently vested in the Government. The suit land was leased out one Abdul Baten in E.P. Case No. 210 of 1967 and subsequently lease was granted to Rahmant-E-Alam Islam Mission who also paid lease Money up 1385 B.S. It is further alleged that the defendant obtained an exparte decree in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 on 6.5.1980 declaring that the suit land is not vested property claiming the suit land as their purchased land from Rathindra Nath Basak who was the adopted son of Debendra Nath Basak by registered kabalas dated 21.7.1977. The Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka was impleaded as a party in the said suit but the Assistant Custodian of the vested and non-resident property was not impleaded in the suit as a party in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 and thus exparte decree dated 5.6.1980 is illegal, void and not binding on the plaintiff. 

 3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing a written statement contending that the suit land originally belonged to Devendra Nath Basak, Lal Mohan Basak and Promotha Nath Basak and by an amicable partition the suit land fell in the Saham of Debendra Nath Basak, one of the sons of Modon Mohan Basak who got 4 annas share in the suit land and the said Dabendra Nath Basak died without any issue but leaving behind only a widow who adopted a son named Rathindra Nath Basak and the suit land was recorded in the name of Rathindra Nath Basak on mutating S.A. Khatian and the defendants purchased the suit land from Rathindra Nath Basak by 11 separate registered kabalas on 21.7.1977 and got their names mutated. The defendant was compelled to file Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 impleading the present plaintiff also as one of the defendants. The summons were duly served on all the defendants but none appeared to contest the suit and ultimately the suit was decreed exparte on 5.6.1980. The defendants then filed an application for correction of the S.A. record before the Circle Officer (Revenue) on the basis of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 and when the matter was placed before the Circle Officer he refused the proposal for correction on the ground that the suit land was declared as enemy property. The defendants alleged that they did not know anything about the treatment of the suit land as enemy property and then made a prayer for releasing the suit land from the list of vested property. It is also alleged that Rathindra Nath Basak never left for India and the suit have could not be declared or treated as enemy or vested property. 

 The trial court framed necessary issues and on consideration of the evidence on record came to the finding that the defendants and to prove their case that Rathindra Nath Basak was a legally adopted son and became the owner of the property of Debendra Nath Basak and unless this could be proved by the defendants, The plaintiff's case that the C.S. and S.A. recorded tenants do not reside in the country and accordingly the property was rightly declared as enemy and then vested property stated proved. The trial court further found that the plaintiffs of the earlier suit were not in possession of the entire suit land and in the earlier suit they were required to pray for recovery of possession and since no such prayer was made, the decree as obtained by fraud. The trial court further found that summons of the earlier suit might be served on the A.D.C. Revenue but that does not mean that the summon was served on the superintendent of vested and non-resident property. The trial Court accordingly came to the conclusion that though government was made a party but the enemy property and vested property authority was not impleaded in the earlier sit and the earlier suit was therefore bad for non-joinder of necessary parties. The trial court further found that Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 was barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and finally concluded that the exparte decree obtained in Title suit No. 346 of 1977 was obtained by fraudulent means. Accordingly by judgment and decree dated 28.6.1992 the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff. 

 5. The defendants then preferred Title Appeal No. 357 of 1992 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka. The learned 8th Court of the Additional District Judge, Dhaka who heard the said appeal found that the plaintiff could not prove that the suit land become enemy and vested property or that the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 was a fraudulent one. The lower appellate court held that the burden of proof lies on the plaintiff to prove that the suit property became enemy property and subsequently vested in the government. The lower appellate court further noticed that fraud and non-joinder of party are not similar and for non- joinder of party it cannot be held that the suit was vitiated by fraud. The learned Additional District Judge further noticed that the plaintiff must prove fraud as they pleaded fraud in the plaint and this not having been proved, the trial court committed error of law in holding that non-joinder of the superintendent, vested and non-resident property has rendered the suit as nullity upon mis-conception of law. Accordingly by judgment and decree dated 30.5.1999 the learned Additional District Judge allowed the appeal, reversed the decision of the trial court and dismissed the plaintiffs suit. 

 6. Being aggrieved thereby the plaintiff being Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka and in charge of vested and non-resident property, Dhaka District as petitioner obtained the present rule. The proforma defendant No. 12 Secretary, Rahmat-E-Alam Islam Mission and Etimkhana as petitioner has obtained another rule being Civil Revision No. 2974 of 1999. 

 8. Mr. Md. Rafiul Alam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in Civil Revision No. 3992 of 1999 has taken me through the judgment of both the courts below and the evidence on record, both oral and documentary including the plaint of the earlier Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 Ext. 6 and submits that the original owner Priaya Nath died leaving behind 4 sons in Nipendra Nath Basak, Nagendra Nath Basak, Digendra Nath basak and Bupendra Nath Basak and the suit land was recorded owners left the country for India in 1965 during Indo-Pak War and the suit land was declared as enemy property and subsequently the same vested in the government as vested and non-resident property. Mr. Chowdhury also submits that the bested property authority has granted lease of the suit land in favour for one Abdul Baten and subsequently in favour for the defendant No. 12 who has been in possession of the suit land on payment of yearly rent. Mr. Chowdhury further submits that the defendant of the present suit-admitted in his evidence that during the earlier suit they were not in possession of the suit land and thus the earlier suit was barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act and the decree obtained in the earlier suit was therefore a fraudulent decree. Mr. Chowdhury further submits that the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) in charge of vested and non resident property was not impleaded in the earlier Title. Suit No. 346 of 1977 and thus the decree obtained in the earlier suit was a fraudulent decree so far it relates to the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), vested and non-resident property. The learned Advocate further submits that the present defendants, who were plaintiffs in Title Suit no. 346 of 1977, could not prove that Rathindra Nath Basak was legally adopted by the widow of debendra Nath Basak and thus Rathindra Nath Basak had no legal right to transfer the suit land to the plaintiffs of the earlier suit. Mr. Chowdhury submits that all these facts were not disclosed in the plaint of the earlier suit and thus the earlier suit was barred under order 6 rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his submission the learned Advocate has relied on a decision in the case of Md. Ibrahim Vs. Md. Alauddin and others reported in 27 DLR 413. With regard to the enemy property, Mr. Chowdhury has relied on a decision in the case of M/s. Dulichand Omaraolal Vs. Bangladesh, through the secretary, Ministry of Industries and others reported in 33 DLR(AD)30 and Enemy property Management Board and others Vs. Abdul Rashid reported in 27 DLR (AD) 52. 

 10. Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner in C.R. No. 2974 of 1999 adopts the submissions of the learned Advocate Mr. Md. Rabiul Alam Chowdhury and added that in the plaint of the earlier Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 the cause of action for the suit was mentioned as dated 21.7.1977 which was the date of the alleged transfers by 11 kabalas by Rathindra Nath basak in favour of the plaintiffs of the earlier suit and this clearly shows that the decree was obtained by practicing fraud upon the court. Dr. Rahman further submits that Rathindra Nath Basak was not a recorded owner of the S.A. Khatian and that the earlier suit was filed on the found of wrong record of the suit land which clearly indicate that the suit land was transferred by Rathindra Nath Basak who was not legally entitled to make any transfer of the suit land on 21.7.1977 when the suit land was treated as vested and non-resident property and was leased out to the petitioner (defendant No. 12) Dr. Rahman also submits that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal but ondidly admits that he has no leg to stands unless the plaintiff succeeds in the suit and the suit land remains vested and non-resident property. 

 12. I have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for both the parties and perused the judgments and the evidence on record. The present petitioner, Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Dhaka and in charge of vested property instituted the suit clearly claiming that all the S.A. recorded owners namely, Nipendra Nath Basak, Nagendra Nath Basak, Digendra Nath Basak and Ehupendra Nath Basak, all sons of Priaya Nath Basak left for India sometimes in 1965 and the suit property became enemy and vested property. It is not denied that in the C.S. and S.A. Khatian the suit land stood recorded in the names of Nipendra Nath Basak, Digandra Nath Basak and Bhupendra Nath Basak and this is the finding and the trial court also. The plaintiff has not admittedly produced the census list or any other material document to indicate that the suit land was declared enemy property after the enemy property law came into force on 3rd of December 1965. The plaintiff has examined one Md. Shamsul Hoque, and Assistant of the vested property of Dhaka and he admitted that they have census list in the office but did not produce the same in court. This P.W. 1 further admitted that they granted lease in respect of 13.17 acres of land to defendant No. 12 on 9.4.1970 Ext. 3 and lease was renewed up 1975. P.W. 1 has produced Ext. 5 showing that lease in favour of defendant No. 12 was renewed up 1396 B.S. This P.W. 1 also admitted in his evidence that the present defendant obtained an exparte decree in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 on 5.6.1980 and the vested property authority was not impleaded or no summon was served on them. This P.W. 1 also admitted in his evidence that in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 the Deputy Commissioner was added as a party and the summon was sent to the section of the Deputy Commissioner, but it was not transmitted to vested property section. This P.W.1 deposed on 1.2.1999 and was not supported or corroborated by any other independent witness to prove that all the S.A. recorded owners left for India in 1965 and did not return to this country. D.W. 2 is one Md. Nur Hossain and he is superintendent of Rahmat-E-Alam Islam Mission and Etimkhana. This D.W.2 deposed to prove that they took lease of portion of the suit land from the vested property authority and they were not party in the earlier Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 Ext. Uma Uma(1) is Memo No. 723 V. P. Dated 17.7.1981 in clearance case No. 2 of 1981 within Tejgoan which shows that 9.47 acres of land appertaining to khatian No. 438,444,798 and 455 were not enlisted property and were not leased out to anybody. The Plaintiff therefore failed to prove either by documentary evidence or by oral evidence that the recorded owners of the S.A. Khatian left the country for India in 1965 and the suit land was declared as enemy property or the same was treated as enemy property. Ext. Uma Uma (1) shows that 9.47 acres out of 20.18 acres of the suit land was never declared vested property or enlisted as vested property or was ever leased out to anyone else. The established principle of law that the plaintiff is to prove his own case and cannot get any relief on the weakness of the defence case is not in any way disputed. The petitioner being Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue) in charge of vested and non-resident property may claim locus standi to challenge the decree passed in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 only when he can prove that the suit land became enemy property and subsequently vested in the government. Unless the suit land became enemy property and vested in the government, the Additional Deputy Commissioner, (Revenue) has no locus standi to challenge the decree passed in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977. The Plaintiff has produced papers showing granting lease of the suit land to some persons including the defendant No. 1 but these papers are not sufficient to come to the conclusion that the suit land was legally declared or enlisted as enemy property and subsequently vested in the government. It is on record being Ext. Uma Uma(1) that 9.47 acres out of total suit land measuring 20.18 acres was never enlisted as vested property and also was never leased out to anyone else. There is therefore complete absence of evidence indicating that the S.A. recorded owners of the suit land left for India in 1965 and 4 the suit land became enemy property and subsequently vested in the government. We are here not sitting over an appeal against the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 346 of 1997 and we are not permitted to decide whether the said suit was barred under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. The lower appellate court has noticed that the plaintiff could not prove that the suit land became enemy property and then vested in the government. The lower appellate court held "on perusing the Id. lower court's judgment I think they failed to prove that the suit property was enemy property and vested to the Government" with regard to non-inclusion of Additional Deputy Commissioner (revenue) in charge of vested and non-resident property in the earlier Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 it is available from record that after obtaining the exparte decree in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 on 5.6.1980 the plaintiff of the earlier suit went to mutate their names through the S.D.O. Dhaka when the circle Officer (Revenue) made a note that the names of the plaintiffs could not be mutated as the suit land was recorded as vested and non-resident property and that was the knowledge of the plaintiffs of the earlier suit with regard to the vested property and non-resident property and they made a representative for releasing the suit land. We do not find anything on record to indicate when the vested property case was started in respect of the suit land but from the evidence on record it is found that Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 was decreed exparte on 5.6.1980 for declaration of title and after the decree the plaintiff of the earlier suit attempted to mutate their names in the record-on-right when it was noticed that the suit land was treated as vested and non-resident property. This will be sometimes after 1980 as the exparte decree was passed on 5.6.1980 as the law on enemy property itself died with the repeal of Ordinance 1 of 1969 with effect from 23.3.74 and no further vested property case could be started thereafter. In that view of the matter the plaintiff having failed to prove that the S.A. Recorded tenants left for India in 1965 and the suit land become enemy property, I am of the view that the plaintiff has no locus standi to challenge the decree passed in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977. Again the P.W. 1 admitted that summons of Title Suit No. 346 of 1977 was served on the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka. There is no evidence of any fraud practiced upon the party or upon the court in obtaining the decree in Title Suit No. 346 of 197. Non-inclusion of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) in charge of vested property is not a fraudulent act to turn down the earlier decree on the ground of fraud as rightly held by the lower appellate court that non-joinder of a party may not defeat the suit in all cases. I have examined the documentary evidence and the oral evidence but I could not find out any material indicating that any fraud was practiced upon the party or the court in obtaining the decree in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977. The learned Advocate for the petitioners could not point out any evidence indicating fraud committed by the plaintiffs of the earlier suit in obtaining the earlier exparte decree. I do not, therefore, find any error of law committed by the lower appellate court in dismissing the plaintiff's suit. The trial court made a totally wrong approach to the pleadings of the parties and the evidence on record and proceeded to decide the legally or otherwise of the decree passed in Title Suit No. 346 of 1977. Non-inclusion of a party cannot be construed as a fraud and decree of a court against a party not impleaded in the suit shall not be turned town on the ground of fraud.
